stages.title: SUBORDINATE ENRICHMENT — ONLY AFTER THE COMPLETE CORE

pills.text: INDIA'S STRUGGLE FOR INDEPENDENCE PRESENTS MILITANT NATIONALISM AS ROOTED
MODERATE POLITICS, OFFICIAL REPRESSION, ECONOMIC HARDSHIP AND A CHANGING
EXTREMISTS EMPHASISED SWARAJ , SELF-CONFIDENCE, SACRIFICE, BOYCOTT, PASSIVE RESISTANCE
NATIONAL EDUCATION RATHER THAN RELIANCE ON BRITISH LIBERAL CONSCIENCE.
TILAK'S PUBLIC FESTIVALS, BANKIM'S VANDE MATARAM , VIVEKANANDA'S MESSAGE
AND AUROBINDO'S POLITICAL WRITINGS FED A LANGUAGE OF ASSERTIVE
EXTREMISM DID NOT SIMPLY REPLACE MODERATE NATIONALISM; IT RADICALISED

groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: India's Struggle for Independence presents militant nationalism as rooted in dissatisfaction with
Moderate politics, official repression, economic hardship and a changing international psychological climate.
Extremists emphasised swaraj , self-confidence, sacrifice, boycott, passive resistance and
national education rather than reliance on British liberal conscience.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: Tilak's public festivals, Bankim's Vande Mataram , Vivekananda's message of strength
and Aurobindo's political writings fed a language of assertive nationalism.
CAUTION: Extremism did not simply replace Moderate nationalism; it radicalised existing economic critique and expanded methods of political action.
Swadeshi mobilised students, women, urban middle classes, zamindars in parts of Bengal, workers

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: in select strikes and sections of rural society through samitis and cultural networks.
Its constructive programme included indigenous industry, arbitration courts, national schools and physical-culture organisations.
Government repression, internal disagreements, limited peasant mobilisation and the Moderates-Extremists
split contributed to decline after the initial high tide.
